section_1.title: Prerequisites & Intuition: From Discrete to Continuous
section_1.content: Briefly recall discrete probability (histograms). Transition to continuous variables by imagining shrinking histogram bin widths toward zero. Introduce the transition from 'bars' to a 'smooth curve'.
section_1.example: Visual transition: A histogram of height measurements gradually becomes a smooth bell-shaped line as we collect millions of data points.

section_2.title: Defining the Probability Density Function (PDF)
section_2.content: Define PDF (f(x)). Crucial realization: f(x) is NOT probability; it is density. Explain that probability corresponds to the 'area under the curve' (the integral).
section_2.example: Analogy: If density is a cloud of gold dust, the probability is the amount of gold inside a specific box, not the height of the cloud at one point.

section_3.title: Core Properties & Visual Constraints
section_3.content: Highlight two mathematical laws: 1) f(x) >= 0 (no negative probability density); 2) Total area under the curve must equal 1 (the 'Total Certainty' rule).
section_3.example: Visual animation: A 'Total Probability' container filling up with water to exactly 1 liter. If we stretch the curve, it must compress in height to keep the volume constant.

section_4.title: Applied Example: The Robot's Battery Life
section_4.content: Demonstrate finding the probability of an event using a specific PDF. Calculate the likelihood of a robot battery dying between 4 and 6 hours by shading the area under the curve.
section_4.example: A robot named 'Bolt' has a battery life modeled by a specific function. We shade the region between x=4 and x=6 to visualize the probability Bolt will stop working during that window.

section_5.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
section_5.content: Recap: Area = Probability. Remind that f(x) at a single point is 0, but the integral over an interval gives the likelihood. Close with the concept of normalization.
section_5.example: Quick 'Flashcard' screen: A summary graphic showing a shaded area on a plot with the formula P(a < X < b) = ∫[a,b] f(x)dx.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.9
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

section_1.title: Prerequisites & Intuition: From Discrete to Continuous
section_1.content: Briefly recall discrete probability (histograms). Transition to continuous variables by imagining shrinking histogram bin widths toward zero. Introduce the transition from 'bars' to a 'smooth curve'.
section_1.example: Visual transition: A histogram of height measurements gradually becomes a smooth bell-shaped line as we collect millions of data points.

section_2.title: Defining the Probability Density Function (PDF)
section_2.content: Define PDF (f(x)). Crucial realization: f(x) is NOT probability; it is density. Explain that probability corresponds to the 'area under the curve' (the integral).
section_2.example: Analogy: If density is a cloud of gold dust, the probability is the amount of gold inside a specific box, not the height of the cloud at one point.

section_3.title: Core Properties & Visual Constraints
section_3.content: Highlight two mathematical laws: 1) f(x) >= 0 (no negative probability density); 2) Total area under the curve must equal 1 (the 'Total Certainty' rule).
section_3.example: Visual animation: A 'Total Probability' container filling up with water to exactly 1 liter. If we stretch the curve, it must compress in height to keep the volume constant.

section_4.title: Applied Example: The Robot's Battery Life
section_4.content: Demonstrate finding the probability of an event using a specific PDF. Calculate the likelihood of a robot battery dying between 4 and 6 hours by shading the area under the curve.
section_4.example: A robot named 'Bolt' has a battery life modeled by a specific function. We shade the region between x=4 and x=6 to visualize the probability Bolt will stop working during that window.

section_5.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
section_5.content: Recap: Area = Probability. Remind that f(x) at a single point is 0, but the integral over an interval gives the likelihood. Close with the concept of normalization.
section_5.example: Quick 'Flashcard' screen: A summary graphic showing a shaded area on a plot with the formula P(a < X < b) = ∫[a,b] f(x)dx.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Key Takeaways", [
            "Area under the curve equals probability.",
            "Single point probability is always zero.",
            "Normalization ensures total area is one."
        ])
        
        # Define graphics
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 1.5, 0.5], x_length=4, y_length=3, axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-(x-2)**2 / 0.5), x_range=[0, 4])
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[1, 3], color=BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        formula = MathTex(r"P(a < X < b) = \int_{a}^{b} f(x)dx", font_size=28)
        norm_text = MathTex(r"\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)dx = 1", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
